questions.question: If a package is not clearly unsafe, what does a driver need to accept hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: You may accept the shipper's certification that a package was properly packed, unless the package is clearly unsafe or does not follow hazardous materials rules.

questions.question: During an inspection, what is the most important thing to check on a tank vehicle?
questions.explanation: Check for leaks on any tank. Transporting gas or liquid in a leaking tank is illegal.

questions.question: Carry-on bags should be placed:

options.text: In front of the back door
In front of the front door
Where they do not block emergency exits

questions.correctAnswerText: Where they do not block emergency exits
questions.explanation: Baggage must not block doorways or aisles. Baggage must be secured so it cannot fall, so the driver can move freely, so passengers can exit through any door or window in an emergency, and so it cannot injure passengers if it shifts.

questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify that the package:

options.text: Was packed at a specific location
Will be placed on the trailer first

questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify that the package follows all required rules.

questions.question: Hazardous materials containers must be:

options.text: Secured so they do not move during transport

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so they do not move during transport
questions.explanation: Secure containers so they will not fall, slide, or move during transport. All hazardous materials packages must be secured.

questions.question: A bridge formula:

options.text: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together
Is not a concern for drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together
questions.explanation: A bridge formula sets lower maximum weight limits for axles that are close together.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be transported with:
questions.explanation: Do not use cargo heaters when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: Before driving, access panels should be:
questions.explanation: Before driving, close all emergency exits and access panels during your outside inspection.

questions.question: When loading cargo onto a vehicle:

options.text: Another person can load it, and they become responsible for cargo safety
Another person can load it, but the driver is responsible for cargo safety
A professional loader must do it

questions.correctAnswerText: Another person can load it, but the driver is responsible for cargo safety
questions.explanation: Even if someone else loads the cargo, the driver is responsible for checking that it is properly loaded and secured, and that it does not block the driver's view or access to emergency equipment.

questions.question: A person supervising tank loading must:

options.text: Not know the materials being loaded
Stay within 25 feet of the tank

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within 25 feet of the tank
questions.explanation: A qualified person must watch the loading of hazardous materials into a tank. This person must stay alert, be able to see the tank, stay within 25 feet of the tank, know the hazards of the materials, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: When stopped at a railroad crossing, how can a bus driver hear if a train is coming?

options.text: Wait for passengers to be quiet on their own.

questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track. Look both ways for a train. Open the front door if it helps you see or hear an oncoming train.

questions.question: What does cargo blocking do?

options.text: Puts cargo in a large box
Stops cargo from sliding during transport
Stops others from buying the cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops cargo from sliding during transport
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing stop cargo from moving during transport.

questions.question: Buses must never carry:
questions.explanation: Buses may carry some hazardous materials under certain conditions. However, they can never carry tear gas or irritating materials.

questions.question: How do other drivers know when hazardous materials are being transported?

options.text: The driver waving an arm out the window

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They warn other drivers about the materials inside.

questions.question: If a vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives is in a collision, the driver should:

options.text: Keep explosives in the vehicle until after separating the vehicles.
Remove explosives from the vehicle before separating the vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove explosives from the vehicle before separating the vehicles.
questions.explanation: In a collision involving Class 1 explosives, warn others of danger and keep people away. Do not allow smoking or open fires. Remove all explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and any buildings.

questions.question: A hazardous waste manifest must:

options.text: Be attached to the outside of the trailer.

questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous waste, you must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. It must be signed by hand.

questions.question: What type of product is usually transported in unbaffled tanks?
questions.explanation: Baffles make a tank hard to clean. Regulations require unbaffled tanks to transport food products like milk.

questions.question: A vehicle without proper placards:

options.text: Can only be moved in an emergency.
Can be driven if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper placards for hazardous materials cannot be driven, except as needed to protect life and property in an emergency.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials:

options.text: Keep all other vehicles away from the station.

questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Someone must always watch the nozzle and control the fuel flow while refueling.

questions.question: A posted speed limit for cars:

options.text: May be too fast for buses.
May be too slow for buses.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be too fast for buses.
questions.explanation: On curves especially, a posted speed limit safe for cars may be too fast for buses. Be extra careful on wet or snowy roads.
